title: PowerShell here-string -- the clean multiline input method (commit messages, AI prompts)
desc: How to pass MULTILINE text in PowerShell with zero escaping, via a here-string. The native answer to multiline commit messages, multiline AI-CLI prompts, and file content -- avoids the bash-to-cmd-to-powershell newline corruption that forces heredocs. Recalled by Haiku 2026-06-10.
steps: WHAT: a PowerShell HERE-STRING is the clean way to pass MULTILINE text (git commit messages, prompts to claude/codex/agy, file content) with ZERO escaping. Two forms, both span lines.

LITERAL form (preferred for prompts and commit messages): open with at-sign then a single-quote as the LAST token on the line, then your raw multi-line text where dollar-signs and backticks stay LITERAL (no expansion), then close with a single-quote then at-sign. Use this whenever the text contains literal dollar signs.

INTERPOLATING form: identical but uses a DOUBLE-quote instead of the single-quote (open at-doublequote, close doublequote-at). PowerShell EXPANDS dollar-variables and backtick escapes inside -- use ONLY when you actually want substitution.

THE GOTCHA (parse error if violated): the opening delimiter must be the LAST token on its line, and the CLOSING delimiter must sit at COLUMN 0 -- no leading whitespace, on its own line. Indenting the closer is a syntax error. This is the single most common mistake.

USE CASES: a literal here-string after git commit -m for multi-line messages; piping a multi-line prompt into an AI CLI without escaping; writing multi-line file content. Pairs with codex-tool-wrappers (the heredoc equivalent for bash-side Agent.cmd).

SEE ALSO (reflex back-link 2026-06-11): ps-script-mojibake-is-output-encoding-first-not-argv -- if a .ps1 prints garbled Korean or U+FFFD, suspect the console OUTPUT encoding FIRST (set OutputEncoding=UTF8 at script start) before blaming the bash-to-powershell argv boundary; [Console]::InputEncoding does NOT touch -File positional argv.
